Based on the search results, I found relevant information about Celeste's dash input system:

The game does not set the direction of a dash until its 5th frame, being a leniency mechanic to prevent players from getting a neutral dash by accidentally pressing the dash button before the directional one. This addresses the input buffer frames and direction priority you asked about.

Additionally, attempting to perform an action that's not currently possible will "buffer" (store) the input for the next 4 frames, and if it becomes possible within those 4 frames and the button is still held, Madeline will instantly perform it.

content.text:
Good news: this is already solved in vanilla Celeste, no mod required. Here's what's going on and where the fix lives.

## Why it happens

I pulled the actual dash logic from the game's released `Player.cs` source. Dash direction isn't read at the instant you press Dash — it's captured a frame later, from a continuously-updated `lastAim` field:

```csharp
// Every Update():
lastAim = Input.GetAimVector(Facing);

// In DashCoroutine():
private IEnumerator DashCoroutine() {
    yield return null;              // waits one game-logic frame
    var dir = lastAim;              // *then* reads direction
    ...
    DashDir = dir;
```

`lastAim` comes from the movement axis (`Input.MoveX`/`MoveY`), while the dash trigger comes from a separate `VirtualButton` (`Input.Dash.Pressed`) with its own press/consume/buffer bookkeeping. When Dash and a direction are bound to the *same* physical key, both get latched by the input system at effectively the same instant, but through different code paths with different timing — so the axis hasn't necessarily "caught up" by the frame `DashCoroutine` samples it. The practical symptom is exactly what you're seeing: a same-key dash+direction bind needs the key held a beat longer than a two-key bind does, because the direction read is genuinely staggered by design (this staggering also exists for the unrelated, well-documented "can't dash diagonally" hardware issue people report on non-NKRO keyboards — different cause, same neighborhood of symptom).

## The fix already exists — no mod needed

Celeste's official **v1.4.0.0** patch added exactly this: separate "Advanced" keybind categories in Options → Controls for **Movement-only** and **Dashing-only** directionals. From the official changelog:

> "Added binds for Advanced: Directionals for movement- or dashing-only"

That's the sanctioned fix. You bind dash-direction keys independently from movement keys (they read as their own axis, sampled the same way the Dash button is), which eliminates the cross-system timing gap causing your issue. Look for the "Advanced" toggle/section in the keyboard/controller rebind screen — it's hidden by default because most players never need it.

## If you were stuck on a pre-1.4 copy and had to mod it

Not needed given the above, but for completeness: you'd use Everest (the community mod loader) + MonoMod hooks, not a from-scratch patch. The cleanest approach, grounded in the real source:

- `Player` already exposes `public Vector2? OverrideDashDirection;`, which `DashCoroutine` checks before falling back to `lastAim`. That field exists precisely for this kind of override.
- An Everest module would hook `On.Celeste.Player.Update` (or an IL hook into the private `DashCoroutine` via `MonoMod.RuntimeDetour`), detect the frame where `Input.Dash.Pressed` fires, snapshot the movement axis *that same frame*, and set `player.OverrideDashDirection` for one tick — bypassing the one-frame-later `lastAim` read entirely.
- Expose your own keybinds via `EverestModuleSettings` with `ButtonBinding` fields (this is the standard pattern every settings-UI mod uses), so players configure it like any other mod option.
- `maddie480/ExtendedVariantMode` is the reference codebase to crib patterns from if you go this route — it's the most actively maintained "gameplay tweak via hooks" mod in the ecosystem.

But again: try the Advanced directional binds first, since that's the maintained, in-box answer to exactly this problem.

Sources:
- [Celeste - Changelog](https://www.celestegame.com/changelog.html)
- [v1.4.0.0 Changelog](https://maddymakesgamesinc.itch.io/celeste/devlog/237097/v1400-changelog)
- [Celeste/Source/Player/Player.cs (official partial source release)](https://github.com/NoelFB/Celeste/blob/master/Source/Player/Player.cs)
- [Diagonal Downward Dash Anomaly :: Celeste General](https://steamcommunity.com/app/504230/discussions/0/3377008022028573081/)
- [can't dash up and right with WASD controls - itch.io](https://itch.io/t/894221/cant-dash-up-and-right-with-wasd-controls)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Builds Everest (the Celeste mod loader) from source and installs it into
# CELESTE_PATH, patching the game in place (MiniInstaller backs up the
# original Celeste.exe itself, but Steam can also re-verify/reinstall the
# game from scratch if anything goes wrong).
set -euo pipefail

CELESTE_PATH="${CELESTE_PATH:-/home/v0id/Games/Steam/steamapps/common/Celeste}"
BUILD_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)/.everest-build"

if [ ! -f "$CELESTE_PATH/Celeste.exe" ]; then
  echo "error: Celeste.exe not found at CELESTE_PATH=$CELESTE_PATH" >&2
  exit 1
fi

command -v dotnet >/dev/null || { echo "error: dotnet not on PATH (enter the flake devshell: nix develop)" >&2; exit 1; }
command -v mono >/dev/null || { echo "error: mono not on PATH (enter the flake devshell: nix develop)" >&2; exit 1; }
command -v git >/dev/null || { echo "error: git not on PATH" >&2; exit 1; }

mkdir -p "$BUILD_DIR"

if [ ! -d "$BUILD_DIR/Everest/.git" ]; then
  echo "cloning EverestAPI/Everest..."
  git clone --depth 1 --recurse-submodules https://github.com/EverestAPI/Everest.git "$BUILD_DIR/Everest"
else
  echo "Everest source already present at $BUILD_DIR/Everest, pulling latest..."
  git -C "$BUILD_DIR/Everest" pull --ff-only
fi

cd "$BUILD_DIR/Everest"

echo "building Everest (Release)..."
dotnet build Everest.sln -c Release

MINI_INSTALLER_OUT="$(find . -type f -iname 'MiniInstaller.dll' -path '*Release*' | head -n1)"
if [ -z "$MINI_INSTALLER_OUT" ]; then
  echo "error: could not find built MiniInstaller.dll under $BUILD_DIR/Everest -- inspect the build output above" >&2
  exit 1
fi
MINI_INSTALLER_DIR="$(dirname "$MINI_INSTALLER_OUT")"

echo "staging build output into $CELESTE_PATH..."
cp -r "$MINI_INSTALLER_DIR"/. "$CELESTE_PATH/"

echo "running MiniInstaller against $CELESTE_PATH..."
(cd "$CELESTE_PATH" && mono MiniInstaller.dll)

if [ -f "$CELESTE_PATH/MMHOOK_Celeste.dll" ]; then
  echo "Everest installed: MMHOOK_Celeste.dll present in $CELESTE_PATH"
else
  echo "warning: MiniInstaller finished but MMHOOK_Celeste.dll wasn't found -- check its output above" >&2
fi

Scaffold Everest mod fixing same-key dash+direction race

Player.DashCoroutine samples dash direction one Update frame after the
dash button press (yield return null before reading lastAim), so a tap
short enough to satisfy Dash.Pressed but release before that later
frame falls back to the neutral/facing direction -- reproducible even
with Celeste's own Advanced dashing-only directional binds, since both
virtual buttons still key off the same physical keypress timing.

DashpadModule hooks Player.Update to buffer the last-held aim direction
for a short grace window and feed it into the existing
Player.OverrideDashDirection field for exactly the two Update calls
that matter (press frame + the frame after, where the coroutine
actually consumes it), bypassing the race instead of fighting it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)"
